source: NASA PDS 2012 shape model; Thomas et al. (2013), Fig. 2b
frame: PDS TEMPEL1_2012_PLAN body-fixed, planetocentric latitude and east-positive longitude. Prime meridian passes through the reference crater west of the impact.

entries.name: Deep Impact site
entries.description: Deep Impact struck here on 4 July 2005.
entries.qualification: Approximate location from the PDS shape-model release.

entries.name: S1 smooth region
entries.description: A smooth deposit that widens downslope. Its shape suggests flowing material.
entries.qualification: Approximate location from the published map. The local shape is poorly constrained.

reference.title: Thomas et al. (2013), The nucleus of Comet 9P/Tempel 1: Shape and geology from two flybys, Fig. 2b and §5.2

entries.name: S2 smooth region
entries.description: A smooth deposit beside a scarp that changed between 2005 and 2011.
entries.qualification: Approximate location from the published map. The local shape is poorly constrained.

reference.title: Thomas et al. (2013), The nucleus of Comet 9P/Tempel 1: Shape and geology from two flybys, Fig. 2b and §5.2

entries.name: S3 smooth region
entries.description: A deposit with finger-like edges and pits, interpreted as a flow.
entries.qualification: Approximate location from the published map.

reference.title: Thomas et al. (2013), The nucleus of Comet 9P/Tempel 1: Shape and geology from two flybys, Fig. 2b and §5.2

entries.name: S4 smooth region
entries.description: A smooth area with low mesas and indistinct edges, possibly formed by several flows.
entries.qualification: Approximate location from the published map.

reference.title: Thomas et al. (2013), The nucleus of Comet 9P/Tempel 1: Shape and geology from two flybys, Fig. 2b and §5.2

digitization.method: Read representative interiors from the published cylindrical map; affine axis conversion, east longitude modulo 360, rounded to 0.1 degree. Sampling is about 0.42 degree/pixel; region centres and boundaries are not determined.
